code_quality.description: Dead code: the initial assignment `reason := "contract generation failed after retries"` is never used as the final value. The outer condition (`lastErr != nil || len(validationErrors) > 0`) guarantees that exactly one of the two inner branches (`if lastErr != nil` or `else if len(validationErrors) > 0`) will always execute and overwrite `reason`. The initial string is always discarded.

rs.LastFinalValidation captures the shell-validator result (which has Pass=true when only contracts fail), while rs.LastValidationResult reflects the combined finalPassed status. If contract assertions fail but all shell checks pass, LastFinalValidation.Pass=true contradicts LastValidationResult="pass=false". Downstream consumers that read LastFinalValidation.Pass directly (e.g. EvidenceStage, reporting) will see a misleading true.
code_quality.suggested_fix: Move `rs.LastFinalValidation = &result` to after `finalPassed` is computed, or introduce a wrapper that overrides the Pass field to reflect combined contract+shell status before storing.

code_quality.description: `const validKeys` is declared inside a for-loop body. While Go permits this with no runtime overhead, declaring constants inside loops is non-idiomatic and forces the reader to re-discover the constant on each loop iteration scan. It also causes the constant definition to be hidden inside an else-branch of the error handling.
code_quality.suggested_fix: Move `const validKeys` to function scope, immediately before the retry loop (e.g. after the `specPacket := string(specPacketBytes)` line at line 106).

code_quality.description: spec-packet.md is read from disk (line 83) before the budget check (line 89). When the budget is already exhausted, the file read is wasted I/O. The spec says budget is checked "before the LLM invocation" — moving the check before the spec-packet read satisfies that requirement while also avoiding unnecessary disk access.
code_quality.suggested_fix: Move the budget check block (lines 88–104) to immediately after the `len(scenarios) == 0` early return (line 79), before reading spec-packet.md.

code_quality.description: The `Run` method is ~135 lines long. The retry loop (lines 115–139) and terminal failure handling (lines 141–163) are dense enough to warrant extraction, making the stage's top-level flow readable at a glance and the retry logic independently testable.

`finalPassed := len(failures) == 0 && result.Pass` — the `&& result.Pass` clause is a silent defensive guard: it handles the edge case where the shell validator returns Pass=false but FailedChecks() returns nothing (a malformed validator). Without a comment, this reads as if `result.Pass` adds new information, when it is actually an edge-case fallback.
code_quality.suggested_fix:
Add an inline comment:

finalPassed := len(failures) == 0 && result.Pass // result.Pass guards against validator returning false without specific check failures

code_quality.description: Variable named `yaml` in `TestValidateStage_ContractFailures` shadows the common `yaml` package name. If `gopkg.in/yaml.v3` is imported in this test file in the future, this local variable will cause a compile error or force a rename.

`fakeContractWriter`, `fakeContractEvaluator`, and `fakeFinalValidator` are defined in both `specloop_test` (contract_integration_test.go) and the `stages` package tests (write_contracts_test.go / validate_test.go). Since they are in separate packages, duplication is unavoidable, but the struct shapes are identical. If the interface signatures change, both copies must be updated.
code_quality.suggested_fix: Consider a shared internal test helpers package (e.g. `internal/next/testfakes`) or, if that is too heavy, ensure the duplicated types are co-located in a single `_test.go` file per package with a clear "test double" comment.

spec_alignment.description: rs.LastFinalValidation is set immediately from the shell-check result before contract failures are collected. When contract assertions fail but shell checks pass (result.Pass=true), LastFinalValidation.Pass will be true while the overall validation outcome is false. Any downstream consumer (e.g., EvidenceStage) relying on LastFinalValidation.Pass for pass/fail reporting will incorrectly show 'passed'. rs.FinalValidationPassed and rs.LastValidationResult are computed correctly from finalPassed, but LastFinalValidation.Pass is inconsistent.
spec_alignment.suggested_fix: Either: (a) set rs.LastFinalValidation after computing finalPassed and patch its Pass field: result.Pass = finalPassed; rs.LastFinalValidation = &result, or (b) add a clear code comment at the LastFinalValidation assignment stating it reflects shell-check results only, and ensure EvidenceStage uses FinalValidationPassed or LastValidationResult for the combined outcome.

spec_alignment.description: The final_validation_result event is emitted with Passed: finalPassed, which is computed after all failures are collected (correct). However, this event emission occurs AFTER rs.LastFinalValidation is set with the shell-only result.Pass. If event consumers treat Passed on this event as the authoritative outcome, they will get the correct combined value — but the inconsistency with rs.LastFinalValidation creates a confusing dual source of truth.
spec_alignment.suggested_fix: Document clearly in a code comment that LastFinalValidation.Pass is shell-only and finalPassed/FinalValidationPassed is the combined validation outcome. Consider aligning LastFinalValidation.Pass with finalPassed.

spec_alignment.description: The file_contains failure detail uses the format 'file %q does not contain %q' (path first, then pattern). The spec's scenario example and failure format section show 'pattern X not found in Y' (pattern first, then path). This is cosmetic and does not affect FailureHistory key extraction (which splits on ' — '), but the detail order differs from the spec's stated example: 'contract:subtract-works — file_contains failed: pattern 'func Subtract' not found in calc/calc.go'.
spec_alignment.suggested_fix: Change to: fmt.Sprintf("pattern %q not found in %q", a.FileContains.Pattern, a.FileContains.Path) to match the spec's illustrative format. Apply the same inversion to file_not_contains.

spec_alignment.description: EvidenceDir is not validated as non-empty before attempting to write scenario-contracts.yaml. If WriteContractsStageConfig.EvidenceDir is accidentally left empty (e.g., misconfigured in tests or new pipeline variants), os.WriteFile will attempt to write 'scenario-contracts.yaml' to the current working directory with no clear diagnostic. The spec states: 'If it does not exist, the stage returns an error (infrastructure failure)'.
spec_alignment.suggested_fix: Add an early guard at the top of Run() or before the write: if s.cfg.EvidenceDir == "" { return specloop.NextAction{}, fmt.Errorf("write_contracts: EvidenceDir is not configured (infrastructure failure)") }

spec_alignment.description: AC15 requires WriteContracts uses Sonnet (P1) model tier. The code uses policy.Models.Planner which maps to Sonnet, but there is no dedicated test verifying the contract writer adapter uses the Planner tier. Other adapters (accept, review) have model tier coverage in stage_provider_test.go (e.g., TestRealStageProvider_BuildStages_DefaultTierUsesModelsEvaluator). The contract writer adapter has no equivalent.
spec_alignment.suggested_fix: Add a test in stage_provider_test.go that verifies the contract writer's LLM adapter is configured with policy.Models.Planner, following the pattern of existing model tier tests in that file.

spec_alignment.description:
On each retry, the spec packet is rebuilt as: '# Prior LLM Error
' + lastErr.Error() + '

' + string(specPacketBytes). This correctly resets to the original spec packet with a prefixed error each attempt (no error accumulation). However, for vocabulary violations, validation errors from the CURRENT attempt are prepended but the code uses 'validationErrors' which is reset at the top of each loop iteration (validationErrors = nil). This means if attempt N has validation errors and attempt N+1 has an LLM error, the blocked reason will correctly reflect the LLM error, not the stale validation errors. This subtle reset-before-assignment pattern is tested by TestWriteContracts_StaleValidationErrorsResetEachIteration, which is good. No code change needed, but the pattern warrants the existing test coverage.
spec_alignment.suggested_fix: No change needed. The existing TestWriteContracts_StaleValidationErrorsResetEachIteration test covers this correctly. Consider adding a comment in the retry loop: '// validationErrors is reset at the top of each iteration to avoid stale state.'
